questions.questionText: A group of students voted on five after-school activities. The bar graph shows the number of students who voted for each of the five activities. How many students chose activity 3?
questions.approach: Find the bar for activity 3 and trace a horizontal line to the y-axis. Do NOT eyeball—look for which answer choice falls in the visible range. The bar sits between gridlines, so eliminate all choices outside that range.
questions.whyRight: The bar for activity 3 reaches a height between 35 and 40. Of the four choices, only 39 falls in that range.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Wrong Scale Trap", "explanation": "25 is below the bar height for activity 3—a misread of the scale or the wrong bar."}, "C": {"name": "Wrong Bar Trap", "explanation": "48 is the count for activity 5, not activity 3. A classic distractor placed next to the correct bar."}, "D": {"name": "Round-Up Trap", "explanation": "50 is the maximum on the graph and appears at activity 5. Overestimating the height of activity 3's bar leads here."}}
questions.patternTip: Bar graphs: trace a horizontal line from the bar top to the y-axis. Then look for the only answer choice in that range—there will always be exactly one.

questions.questionText: What percentage of 300 is 75?
questions.approach: Part ÷ Whole = decimal, then ×100 for percent. 75 ÷ 300 = 0.25 = 25%. Or set up: (x/100)×300 = 75 → x = 25.
questions.whyRight: 75 ÷ 300 = 0.25 = 25%. The part (75) is one-quarter of the whole (300).
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Half-the-Whole Trap", "explanation": "50% of 300 is 150, not 75. A student who estimates roughly without calculating lands here."}, "C": {"name": "Literal Number Trap", "explanation": "The number 75 appears in the question—students assume 75% without checking. Always compute."}, "D": {"name": "Backwards Fraction Trap", "explanation": "225% comes from computing 300/75×100 instead of 75/300×100. Always put the part on top."}}
questions.patternTip: Percent = (part ÷ whole) × 100. Part on top, whole on bottom. 75 ÷ 300 = 25%. If your answer seems too large, you probably flipped the fraction.

questions.questionText: x²/25 = 36. What is a solution to the given equation?
questions.approach: Isolate x². Multiply both sides by 25: x² = 900. Take the square root: x = 30 or x = −30. Match to the choices.
questions.whyRight: x² = 900. √900 = 30. Both 30 and −30 are solutions, but only 30 appears as a choice.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Skipped Multiplication Trap", "explanation": "Taking √36 = 6 without first multiplying by 25. The student solves x²=36 instead of x²/25=36."}, "C": {"name": "Multiplied Without Rooting Trap", "explanation": "25 × 36 = 900 is the right intermediate step, but then the student divides by 2 (getting 450) instead of taking the square root."}, "D": {"name": "Forgot Square Root Trap", "explanation": "900 is the correct value of x²—students who stop before taking the square root report this."}}
questions.patternTip: Two-step process: (1) multiply both sides by 25 to get x²=900, (2) take the square root to get x=30. Missing step 2 is the most common error.

questions.questionText: 3 more than 8 times a number x is equal to 83. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.approach: Translate word by word. '8 times x' → 8x. '3 more than' → add 3 to whatever came before. '3 more than 8x' → 8x + 3. 'Is equal to 83' → = 83.
questions.whyRight: '8 times a number x' = 8x. '3 more than' = +3. Combined: 8x + 3 = 83.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Multiply Instead of Add Trap", "explanation": "(3)(8)x treats '3 more' as multiplication by 3. 'More than' always means addition, never multiplication."}, "B": {"name": "Flip-It Trap", "explanation": "8x = 83 + 3 puts the +3 on the wrong side. The 3 belongs with the x-expression, not with 83."}, "C": {"name": "Swap Trap", "explanation": "3x + 8 = 83 swaps the roles of 3 and 8. The problem says '8 times x,' not '3 times x.'"}}
questions.patternTip: 'More than' = add. '8 times x' = 8x. '3 more than 8 times x' builds left to right: 8x, then +3. The number being multiplied (8) always attaches to x.

questions.questionText: Hana deposited a fixed amount into her bank account each month. The function f(t) = 100 + 25t gives the amount, in dollars, in Hana's bank account after t monthly deposits. What is the best interpretation of 25 in this context?
questions.answerChoices: {"A": "With each monthly deposit, the amount in Hana's bank account increased by $25.", "B": "Before Hana made any monthly deposits, the amount in her bank account was $25.", "C": "After 1 monthly deposit, the amount in Hana's bank account was $25.", "D": "Hana made a total of 25 monthly deposits."}
questions.approach: In f(t) = b + mt, m is the rate of change (what happens each time t increases by 1) and b is the starting value (when t = 0). Here 25 is the coefficient of t → it's the per-deposit increase.
questions.whyRight: The coefficient 25 is attached to t (the number of deposits). Each additional deposit increases the account by $25.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Constant Confusion Trap", "explanation": "The starting value (t=0) is 100, not 25. Choice B describes the constant term, not the coefficient."}, "C": {"name": "Evaluate Wrong Trap", "explanation": "f(1) = 100 + 25(1) = 125, not 25. This confuses the coefficient with the output."}, "D": {"name": "Variable-as-Answer Trap", "explanation": "25 is a coefficient, not the number of deposits. t represents the number of deposits, not 25."}}
questions.patternTip: Linear function y = b + mx: b = starting value, m = rate of change per unit of input. 25 is attached to t, so it tells you what happens each time t goes up by 1.

questions.questionText: A customer spent $27 to purchase oranges at $3 per pound. How many pounds of oranges did the customer purchase?
questions.approach: Total cost ÷ cost per unit = number of units. $27 ÷ $3 per pound = 9 pounds.
questions.whyRight: 9 pounds × $3/pound = $27. Division confirms the answer.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Multiply Trap": {"name": "Multiply Trap", "explanation": "Multiplying 27 × 3 = 81 inverts the operation. You need to divide total by rate."}, "Subtract Trap": {"name": "Subtract Trap", "explanation": "Subtracting 27 − 3 = 24 uses the wrong operation entirely."}}
questions.patternTip: Unit rate problems: divide the total by the per-unit cost. 'How many at $3 each?' = total ÷ 3.

questions.questionText: Nasir bought 9 storage bins that were each the same price. He used a coupon for $63 off the entire purchase. The cost for the entire purchase after using the coupon was $27. What was the original price, in dollars, for 1 storage bin?
questions.approach: Undo the coupon first: $27 + $63 = $90 (pre-coupon total). Then divide by 9 bins: $90 ÷ 9 = $10.
questions.whyRight: $27 (paid) + $63 (coupon) = $90 total before discount. $90 ÷ 9 = $10 per bin.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Ignore Coupon Trap": {"name": "Ignore Coupon Trap", "explanation": "Dividing $27 ÷ 9 = $3 ignores the coupon. The pre-coupon total must be found first."}, "Coupon Only Trap": {"name": "Coupon Only Trap", "explanation": "Dividing $63 ÷ 9 = $7 uses only the coupon amount, not the full purchase price."}}
questions.patternTip: Multi-step discount problems: always undo the discount first (add it back), then divide. The coupon reduced the total—reverse that before finding the per-unit price.

questions.questionText: For the linear function f, the table shows three values of x and their corresponding values of f(x): x=0 → f(x)=29; x=1 → f(x)=32; x=2 → f(x)=35. Which equation defines f(x)?
questions.approach: Find slope: f(1) − f(0) = 32 − 29 = 3. Find y-intercept: f(0) = 29. Plug into y = mx + b: f(x) = 3x + 29.
questions.whyRight: Slope = 3 (difference between consecutive outputs). Y-intercept = 29 (the value when x = 0). Equation: f(x) = 3x + 29.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Swap and Negate Trap", "explanation": "29x − 3 puts 29 as the slope and makes b negative. The slope is 3 (the difference), not 29."}, "C": {"name": "Wrong Intercept Trap", "explanation": "3x + 32 uses f(1) = 32 as the y-intercept. The y-intercept is f(0) = 29, not f(1) = 32."}, "D": {"name": "Full Swap Trap", "explanation": "32x + 3 uses f(1) as slope and the slope (3) as intercept—completely reversed."}}
questions.patternTip: Two rules for linear function from table: (1) slope = change in output per 1-unit change in input; (2) y-intercept = output when x = 0. Read f(0) directly from the table.

questions.questionText: Right triangles PQR and STU are similar, where P corresponds to S. Angle R and angle U are right angles. If the measure of angle Q is 18°, what is the measure of angle S?
questions.approach: List the correspondence: P↔S, Q↔T, R↔U. Q corresponds to T, not S. Use only triangle STU: S + 18° + 90° = 180°. Solve: S = 72°.
questions.whyRight: Q and T are corresponding (not Q and S). T = 18°. Triangle STU: S + 18 + 90 = 180 → S = 72°.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Wrong Correspondence Trap", "explanation": "18° is angle T (corresponding to Q), not angle S. Confusing which angles correspond is the central trap."}, "C": {"name": "Arithmetic Error Trap", "explanation": "82° comes from 100° − 18° or similar wrong subtraction—no geometric basis."}, "D": {"name": "Supplement Trap", "explanation": "162° = 90° + 72°, adding the two known angles together instead of subtracting from 180°."}}
questions.patternTip: Write the full correspondence before doing any math: P↔S, Q↔T, R↔U. The question involves angle S (paired with P), not Q. Work only inside triangle STU.

questions.questionText: The scatterplot shows the relationship between two variables x and y, with data points trending downward. Which of the following equations is the most appropriate linear model for the data shown?
questions.approach: Two-filter method: (1) Slope direction—data goes down → negative slope → eliminate A and C. (2) Y-intercept—when x ≈ 0, y ≈ 9–10 → intercept ≈ 9.4 → eliminate B (intercept = 0.9). Only D remains.
questions.whyRight: D has negative slope (−0.9) matching the downward trend, and y-intercept 9.4 matching where the data starts near the y-axis.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Positive Slope Trap", "explanation": "9.4x has a positive slope. Data clearly decreases—any positive slope is wrong."}, "B": {"name": "Intercept Swap Trap", "explanation": "y = 0.9 − 9.4x has negative slope (correct) but y-intercept 0.9 (too small). Intercept and slope values are swapped."}, "C": {"name": "Positive Slope Trap", "explanation": "0.9x has positive slope. Same error as A—ignoring that the data trends downward."}}
questions.patternTip: Scatterplot model selection: two filters, in order. Step 1: slope sign (eliminates 2 choices). Step 2: y-intercept value (eliminates 1 more). You never need to calculate the exact model.

questions.questionText: The given equation 2.5b + 5r = 80 describes the relationship between the number of birds, b, and the number of reptiles, r, that can be cared for at a pet care business on a given day. If the business cares for 16 reptiles on a given day, how many birds can it care for?
questions.approach: Plug In r = 16: 2.5b + 5(16) = 80. 2.5b + 80 = 80. 2.5b = 0. b = 0. Zero is a valid answer—don't dismiss it.
questions.whyRight: 5 × 16 = 80, which exactly fills the right side. Nothing remains for 2.5b, so b = 0.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Arithmetic Slip Trap", "explanation": "5 appears in the equation; students may read it as the answer. Requires an arithmetic error in solving."}, "C": {"name": "Ignore Substitution Trap", "explanation": "80 ÷ 2 = 40. Student divides the constant by the coefficient without substituting r first."}, "D": {"name": "Constant-as-Answer Trap", "explanation": "Simply reading 80 from the equation without doing any calculation."}}
questions.patternTip: Always substitute before simplifying. When r = 16 makes the equation 2.5b + 80 = 80, the b term drops out. Zero birds is a perfectly valid SAT answer.

questions.questionType: Equation of a Line from Graph
questions.questionText: What is an equation of the line shown in the graph, which passes through (−8, 0) and (0, −8)?
questions.approach: Read two points: (0, −8) and (−8, 0). Slope = rise/run = (0 − (−8)) / (−8 − 0) = 8/(−8) = −1. Y-intercept = −8 (where line crosses y-axis). Equation: y = −x − 8.
questions.whyRight: Slope = −1, y-intercept = −8. Equation: y = −(1)x − 8 = −x − 8.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Slope Magnitude Error Trap", "explanation": "−2x − 8 has slope −2. Rise = 8, run = 8 → slope = −1, not −2."}, "B": {"name": "Positive Slope Trap", "explanation": "y = x − 8 has positive slope. The line goes from upper-left to lower-right → slope must be negative."}, "D": {"name": "Positive Slope Trap", "explanation": "y = 2x − 8 has positive slope and wrong magnitude. Both errors: wrong sign and wrong value."}}
questions.patternTip: Line going from upper-left to lower-right = negative slope. Always. Eliminate positive-slope choices first. Then compute: slope = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁) = 8/−8 = −1.

questions.questionText: If x/8 = 5, what is the value of 8/x?
questions.approach: Flip both sides: x/8 = 5 becomes 8/x = 1/5. Done. No need to find x first.
questions.whyRight: Reciprocal of x/8 = 5 gives 8/x = 1/5 directly. Or: x = 40, so 8/40 = 1/5.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Solve-for-x Trap": {"name": "Solve-for-x Trap", "explanation": "Solving for x = 40 then forgetting to compute 8/40, reporting 40 instead."}, "Multiply Trap": {"name": "Multiply Trap", "explanation": "Computing 8 × 5 = 40 instead of 8/40."}, "Repeat Trap": {"name": "Repeat Trap", "explanation": "Reporting 5 as the answer, repeating the given equation's value."}}
questions.patternTip: When asked for the reciprocal of an expression, flip both sides of the equation. x/8 = 5 → 8/x = 1/5. One step, no algebra needed.

questions.questionText: The solution to the system 24x + y = 48 and 6x + y = 72 is (x, y). What is the value of y?
questions.approach: Subtract equation 2 from equation 1 to eliminate y: 18x = −24, so x = −4/3. Substitute back: 6(−4/3) + y = 72 → −8 + y = 72 → y = 80.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Report x Trap": {"name": "Report x Trap", "explanation": "Solving for x and reporting x = −4/3 or −1.33 instead of y. The question asks for y."}, "Sign Error Trap": {"name": "Sign Error Trap", "explanation": "Adding the equations instead of subtracting creates a sign error in the x coefficient."}, "Wrong Equation Trap": {"name": "Wrong Equation Trap", "explanation": "Substituting back into the wrong equation yields a different (incorrect) value."}}
questions.patternTip: The question asks for y. After finding x, immediately substitute to get y. A very common error: reporting x = −4/3 and moving on. Always check which variable is requested.

questions.questionText: Line t in the xy-plane has a slope of −1/3 and passes through the point (9, 10). Which equation defines line t?
questions.approach: Point-slope: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Substitute m = −1/3 and point (9, 10): y − 10 = −(1/3)(x − 9). Distribute: y = −x/3 + 3 + 10 = −x/3 + 13.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Full Swap Trap", "explanation": "y = 13x − 1/3 uses the point's y-coordinate as slope and the slope as y-intercept. Completely reversed."}, "B": {"name": "Coordinate-as-Slope Trap", "explanation": "y = 9x + 10 uses the x-coordinate (9) as the slope. The slope is −1/3."}, "C": {"name": "Wrong Intercept Trap", "explanation": "y = −x/3 + 10 uses y₁ = 10 directly as the intercept. The intercept requires adding the −(1/3)(−9) = +3 term: 10 + 3 = 13."}}
questions.patternTip: Point-slope common pitfall: when distributing m × (−x₁), a negative × negative = positive. Here: −(1/3) × (−9) = +3, so b = 10 + 3 = 13, not 10 − 3 = 7.

questions.questionText: The function f(x) = 206(1.034)^x models the value in dollars of a bank account by the end of each year from 1957 through 1972, where x is the number of years after 1957. Which of the following is the best interpretation of 'f(5) is approximately equal to 243' in this context?
questions.answerChoices: {"A": "The value of the bank account is estimated to be approximately 5 dollars greater in 1962 than in 1957.", "B": "The value of the bank account is estimated to be approximately 243 dollars in 1962.", "C": "The value, in dollars, of the bank account is estimated to be approximately 5 times greater in 1962 than in 1957.", "D": "The value of the bank account is estimated to increase by approximately 243 dollars every 5 years between 1957 and 1972."}
questions.approach: Translate f(5) = 243: input x = 5 → year 1957 + 5 = 1962. Output f(x) = 243 → value is $243. The function maps time to value.
questions.whyRight: x = 5 years after 1957 = 1962. f(5) ≈ 243 means the account is worth about $243 in 1962.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Input-Output Swap Trap", "explanation": "Treats 5 as a dollar amount (output) and 243 as a time period. The roles of input and output are reversed."}, "C": {"name": "Ratio Trap", "explanation": "Interpreting x = 5 as '5 times greater.' x is a year count, not a multiplier."}, "D": {"name": "Rate Trap", "explanation": "Treats 243 as a per-period addition (constant growth), ignoring that the function is exponential—growth is not constant."}}
questions.patternTip: For function interpretation: input (x) = the independent quantity (years), output f(x) = the dependent quantity (dollars). f(5) = 243 → 'at year 5, value is 243.' Never swap input and output.

questions.questionText: For a certain rectangular region, the ratio of its length to its width is 35 to 10. If the width of the rectangular region increases by 7 units, how must the length change to maintain this ratio?
questions.answerChoices: {"A": "It must decrease by 24.5 units.", "B": "It must increase by 24.5 units.", "C": "It must decrease by 7 units.", "D": "It must increase by 7 units."}
questions.approach: The ratio is l/w = 3.5. So l = 3.5w. New width = w + 7 → new length = 3.5(w + 7) = 3.5w + 24.5. Change in length = 24.5 (increase).
questions.whyRight: Length must increase to maintain ratio when width increases. Change in length = 3.5 × 7 = 24.5.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Wrong Direction Trap", "explanation": "Length must increase when width increases to maintain a positive ratio. A decrease would shrink the ratio."}, "C": {"name": "Equal Change Trap", "explanation": "If length also changed by 7, the ratio would shift. The ratio multiplies the change: 7 × 3.5 = 24.5."}, "D": {"name": "Equal Change Trap", "explanation": "Same error: assumes length changes by the same absolute amount as width. The ratio factor (3.5) must be applied."}}
questions.patternTip: When one side of a ratio changes by n, the other must change by n × ratio. Width +7 → length changes by 7 × 3.5 = 24.5. Multiply by the ratio, don't just mirror the change.

questions.questionText: Square P has a side length of x inches. Square Q has a perimeter that is 176 inches greater than the perimeter of square P. The function f gives the area of square Q, in square inches. Which of the following defines f?
questions.approach: Perimeter of Q = 4x + 176. Side of Q = divide by 4: (4x + 176)/4 = x + 44. Area = side² = (x + 44)².
questions.whyRight: Side of Q = (4x + 176) ÷ 4 = x + 44. Area = (x + 44)².
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "No Division Trap", "explanation": "(x + 176)² skips dividing the 176 by 4. The 176 is added to the perimeter, not to the side directly."}, "C": {"name": "Multiply Instead of Divide Trap", "explanation": "(176x + 44)² multiplies x by 176 instead of dividing. Perimeter → side requires division by 4."}, "D": {"name": "Multiple Errors Trap", "explanation": "(176x + 176)² ignores the division by 4 completely—applies 176 directly to both terms."}}
questions.patternTip: Perimeter = 4 × side. To get side from perimeter, divide by 4. Don't add 176 directly to x—add 176 to the perimeter (4x), then divide the whole thing by 4.

questions.questionText: The equation 14x / 7y = 2√(w + 19) relates the distinct positive real numbers w, x, and y. Which equation correctly expresses w in terms of x and y?
questions.approach: Step 1: Simplify 14x/7y = 2x/y. Step 2: Divide both sides by 2 → x/y = √(w+19). Step 3: Square both sides → (x/y)² = w+19. Step 4: Subtract 19 → w = (x/y)² − 19.
questions.whyRight: After simplification and isolation: squaring both sides of x/y = √(w+19) gives (x/y)² = w+19, so w = (x/y)² − 19.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Forgot to Square Trap", "explanation": "Taking the square root instead of squaring: √(x/y) − 19. The step is to SQUARE both sides to eliminate √."}, "B": {"name": "No Simplification Trap", "explanation": "Fails to reduce 14/7 = 2 first, so 14x/7y stays unsimplified → messy expression that isn't among the clean choices."}, "D": {"name": "No Simplification + Square Trap", "explanation": "Combines the unsimplified fraction with squaring. Two errors at once."}}
questions.patternTip: To solve for a variable inside a square root: isolate the radical first (simplify and divide), then square both sides. Skipping the simplification creates ugly expressions that don't match any choice.

questions.questionText: Point O is the center of a circle. The measure of arc RS on this circle is 100°. What is the measure, in degrees, of its associated angle ROS?
questions.approach: Central angle theorem: central angle = intercepted arc. Arc RS = 100° → angle ROS = 100°. Direct application, no calculation needed.
questions.whyRight: Angle ROS is a central angle (vertex at center O). Its measure equals the arc RS = 100°.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Inscribed Angle Trap": {"name": "Inscribed Angle Trap", "explanation": "Computing 100°/2 = 50° confuses the central angle with the inscribed angle theorem. Central angle = arc; inscribed angle = half arc."}, "Major Arc Trap": {"name": "Major Arc Trap", "explanation": "Computing 360° − 100° = 260° uses the major arc instead of the given minor arc."}, "Supplement Trap": {"name": "Supplement Trap", "explanation": "Computing 180° − 100° = 80° incorrectly takes the supplement."}}
questions.patternTip: Central angle = arc. Inscribed angle = half the arc. The central angle has its vertex AT the center. Here O is the center, so angle ROS = arc RS = 100°.

questions.questionText: The expression 6·⁵√(3⁵x⁴⁵)·⁸√(2⁸x) is equivalent to ax^b, where a and b are positive constants and x > 1. What is the value of a + b?
questions.approach: Convert radicals using ⁿ√(x^m) = x^(m/n). ⁵√(3⁵x⁴⁵) = 3·x⁹. ⁸√(2⁸x) = 2·x^(1/8). Multiply everything: 6·3·2·x^(9 + 1/8) = 36·x^(73/8). Then a + b = 36 + 73/8.
questions.whyRight: a = 36 (the constant), b = 73/8 (the x-exponent). a + b = 288/8 + 73/8 = 361/8.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Forget 1/8 Trap": {"name": "Forget 1/8 Trap", "explanation": "Getting a = 36 but then adding 36 + 9 = 45, forgetting the 1/8 from the second radical's x-exponent."}, "Decimal Error Trap": {"name": "Decimal Error Trap", "explanation": "Computing 9 + 1/8 incorrectly as a decimal and rounding wrong."}, "Forget 6 Trap": {"name": "Forget 6 Trap", "explanation": "Forgetting to multiply the 6 into the constant: getting a = 6 instead of 36."}}
questions.patternTip: ⁿ√(x^m) = x^(m/n). When the power matches the root index (3⁵ under a 5th root), it simplifies to just the base. Multiply all constants together first, then add x-exponents.

questions.questionText: A right triangle has sides of length 2√2, 6√2, and √80 units. What is the area of the triangle, in square units?
questions.approach: Verify which side is the hypotenuse using a² + b² = c²: (2√2)² + (6√2)² = 8 + 72 = 80 = (√80)². Hypotenuse = √80. Legs = 2√2 and 6√2. Area = ½·2√2·6√2 = 12.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Perimeter Trap", "explanation": "8√2 + √80 adds two sides together. Area requires multiplication, not addition."}, "C": {"name": "Wrong Formula Trap", "explanation": "Multiplies all three sides (or misapplies ½bh) without the ½ and using the hypotenuse as a leg."}, "D": {"name": "Forgot ½ Trap", "explanation": "2√2 × 6√2 = 12 × 2 = 24. Correct multiplication but forgot the ½ factor for triangle area."}}
questions.patternTip: Right triangle area = ½ × leg₁ × leg₂. First identify the hypotenuse (the longest side) using the Pythagorean theorem. The two LEGS are the base and height—not the hypotenuse.

questions.questionText: The expression 4x² + bx − 45, where b is a constant, can be rewritten as (hx + k)(x + j), where h, k, and j are integer constants. Which of the following must be an integer?
questions.approach: Expand the factored form: constant term = kj = −45. Since h, k, j are all integers, k divides 45, making 45/k = −j an integer. The other ratios (b/h, b/k, 45/h) are not guaranteed.
questions.whyRight: kj = −45, and j is an integer, so k must be a divisor of 45. Therefore 45/k = −j, which is an integer.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Slope-Like Thinking Trap", "explanation": "b/h = (hj + k)/h = j + k/h. k/h is not guaranteed to be an integer since h = 4 doesn't necessarily divide k."}, "B": {"name": "Partial Product Trap", "explanation": "b/k = (hj + k)/k = hj/k + 1. hj/k is not guaranteed to be an integer."}, "C": {"name": "Wrong Factor Trap", "explanation": "45/h = 45/4, which is 11.25—definitely not an integer since 4 does not divide 45."}}
questions.patternTip: The constant term in a factored quadratic = product of the constant terms in the factors (kj = −45). Since both are integers, each must divide 45. That makes 45/k guaranteed to be an integer.

questions.questionText: In the system y = 2x² − 21x + 64 and y = 3x + a, where a is a constant, the graphs intersect at exactly one point. What is the value of x?
questions.approach: Set equal and collect: 2x² − 24x + (64−a) = 0. For one intersection: discriminant = 0. Solve for a = −8. Substitute back: 2x² − 24x + 72 = 0 → (x−6)² = 0 → x = 6.
questions.whyRight: With a = −8, the quadratic becomes (x − 6)² = 0, giving the unique solution x = 6.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Solve-for-a Trap", "explanation": "−8 is the value of a, not x. The question asks for x. Students find a = −8 and stop."}, "B": {"name": "Sign Error Trap", "explanation": "−6 results from a sign error when factoring or applying the quadratic formula."}, "D": {"name": "Positive Root Trap", "explanation": "x = 8 is a plausible-looking answer that comes from an arithmetic error in the discriminant calculation."}}
questions.patternTip: Two-trap question: first you find a = −8 (choice A is a trap), then you find x = 6 (choice C). Always re-read the question: 'What is the value of x?' not 'What is a?'

questions.questionText: An isosceles right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 58 inches. What is the perimeter, in inches, of this triangle?
questions.approach: 45-45-90: leg = hypotenuse/√2 = 58/√2 = 29√2. Perimeter = 29√2 + 29√2 + 58 = 58√2 + 58. ALL THREE sides must be included.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "One Leg Trap", "explanation": "29√2 is the length of one leg. Perimeter requires all three sides."}, "B": {"name": "Two Legs Trap", "explanation": "58√2 = 2 × 29√2, both legs but missing the hypotenuse (58)."}, "D": {"name": "Wrong Ratio Trap", "explanation": "If a student mistakenly uses leg = hypotenuse × √2 (instead of ÷√2), they get each leg = 58√2, and perimeter = 58 + 116√2."}}
questions.patternTip: 45-45-90 ratio: leg = hypotenuse × (√2/2) = hypotenuse ÷ √2. With hypotenuse = 58: each leg = 29√2. The perimeter trap: always add ALL three sides including the hypotenuse.

questions.questionText: In the xy-plane, a parabola has vertex (9, −14) and intersects the x-axis at two points. If the equation of the parabola is written in the form y = ax² + bx + c, where a, b, and c are constants, which of the following could be the value of a + b + c?
questions.approach: Key insight: a + b + c = f(1). Use vertex form: f(x) = a(x−9)² − 14. So f(1) = 64a − 14. Set equal to each choice and check if a > 0 (required since parabola opens upward). Only D works.
questions.whyRight: f(1) = 64a − 14 = −12 → a = 1/32 > 0 ✓. Choices A, B, C give a < 0 (downward parabola, which wouldn't intersect x-axis at two points from below).
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Negative-a Trap", "explanation": "−23 requires a < 0 → parabola opens downward → with vertex at y = −14 (below x-axis) it would have no x-intercepts. Contradicts the problem."}, "B": {"name": "Negative-a Trap", "explanation": "Same logic as A. a < 0 with vertex at −14 → zero x-intercepts."}, "C": {"name": "Vertex y-value Trap", "explanation": "−14 is the y-coordinate of the vertex. Some students confuse a + b + c (which equals f(1)) with the vertex y-value."}}
questions.patternTip: a + b + c = f(1) for any polynomial. Parabola opens upward (vertex below x-axis, two x-intercepts) → a > 0. Use these two facts together to eliminate choices that require a < 0.

questions.questionText: Function f is defined by f(x) = −aˣ + b, where a and b are constants. In the xy-plane, the graph of y = f(x) − 15 has a y-intercept at (0, −99/7). The product of a and b is 65/7. What is the value of a?
questions.approach: At x = 0: −a⁰ = −1 (any base to the 0th power is 1). So b − 16 = −99/7 → b = 13/7. Then a = (65/7) ÷ (13/7) = 5.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Wrong Zero Power Trap": {"name": "Wrong Zero Power Trap", "explanation": "Using a⁰ = a instead of a⁰ = 1 creates unsolvable algebra."}, "Report b Trap": {"name": "Report b Trap", "explanation": "Finding b = 13/7 but then reporting b as the final answer instead of a."}, "Fraction Arithmetic Trap": {"name": "Fraction Arithmetic Trap", "explanation": "Arithmetic errors with fractions: miscomputing 16 − 99/7."}}
questions.patternTip: Critical rule: x⁰ = 1 for ANY base. f(0) = −a⁰ + b = −1 + b. If you write f(0) = −a + b, you'll get stuck with algebra that doesn't resolve cleanly.
